div.head: m,k)-firm model has recently drawn many attentionsfor providing a flexible real-time system with graceful degradation of the QoS. DBP algorithm is an attractive one a s it dynamically assigns the priorities according to the system's current state (QoS-aware scheduling). However DBP cannot readily be used for systems requiring deteministic (mk)-firm guarantee since the schedulability analysis was not done in the original proposition. In this paper a suficient schedulability condition is given to deteministically guarantee a set of periodic or sporadic activities (jobs) sharing a common non-preemptive server. This condition is used for bandwidth dimensioning of the communication system of the distributed control system showing its practical usefulness.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: It is well known that real-time systems designed according to the worst-case condition (case of hard-real time system design) often result in large resources requirement. As at nm time the system is seldom in the worst-case, a large amount of system resources are under utilized. A fmt solution is to design the system considering an average case. This solution can be suitable for a subclass of soft real-time systems requiring only probabilistic deadline guarantee.

However, for other real-time systems such as those found in multimedia and automatic control domain, providing only probabilistic deadline guamntee could be unacceptable. A more precise specification on how the deadline misses are distributed in time is necessary [2] and this can be done using (m,k)-firm model [4].
Typically, for a same deadline miss ratio, a real-time application (e.g. voicelvideo packets transmission) k n e r tolerates non consecutive deadline misses than the consecutive ones.

Comparing to the soft real-time or firm real-time, (m,k)-firm real-time constraint requires further the guarantee (which can be either deterministic, statistic or probabilistic according to the application) of m out of any k consecutive job executions, otherwise, the system is said to be in dynamic failure state. Using this (m,k)-firm model, a system can then be designed to tolerate missed deadlines provided that this number of missed deadlines is bounded and even precisely distributed in time. This (m,k)-fm model also allows the design of the adaptive real-time systems providing dynamic QoS (Quality of Service) management [I]. In fact a system offering (m,k)-firm guarantee ensures a minimum QoS of m out of k deadlines met in the worst-case. In general cases, more than m deadlines could be met as the system does not always run in the worst-case load condition. From classical hard realtime system designer's point of view, using (m,k)-fm approach allows to introduce the notion of "graceful degradation of the Q o S . Finally, note that, as like as for hard real-time, sufficient conditions of feasibility are obviously required in order to ensure a deterministic (m&)-firm guarantee. The rationale for considering the dynamic (m,k)fm scheduling algorithms, is bdsed on the following reasons. We assume that, for the targeted application (multimedia, networked control systems), constraints are expressed according to the (m,k)-fim model. For on-line ensuring these properties, the system should be adaptive to workload variation (e.g. in networks handling QoS with connection admission control) by taking advantage of the possibility to discard until k-m out of k consecutive jobs during the system overload periods. So, in this context, an off-tine scheduling is simply not suitable. Furthermore, the use of a dynamic scheduling policy allows in general a better exploitation of the available resources than the use of a static scheduling one.

Once we established that a dynamic policy is best suited to the application requirements, we have to justify the choice of DBP face to DWCS. We recall, that for the targeted applications, we have to exhibit at least a sufficient feasibility condition. For DWCS such a condition was established in [12]; but it has a limited application region since the jobs must be with the same service time and the same periods. That is why, although DBP itself' is still improvable [7], we investigated this policy in order to find a more genenl condition. Moreover as we would like to obtain a result applicable both to CPU tasks scheduling and network packets scheduling, we further restrict our self to the non-preemptive scheduling. As proposed in the former studies [4], [12], we consider EDF for priority equality cases.
Therefore in this paper we only focus on NP-DBP-

The resulting priority contributes then to maintain the global performance of the system. When m is equal to k, an (m,k)-firm constraint becomes a strict hard realtime one. However a server capacity dimensioned using this condition would be oversize, as it does not take profit of the possibility to drop k-m out of k consecutive instances. So in order to face to this problem, we apply a rationale similar to those done for Jeffay's theorem in order to obtain a sufficient condition for NP-DBP-EDF. This is the purpose of the next section.

div.head: Sufficient Condition For NP-DBP-EDF
div.p: Unlike hard real-time (HRT) scheduling, for (m6)fm scheduling there does not exist a condition which is both necessary and sufficient. In [7] we have given a necessary condition for NP-DBP-EDF. But this necessary condition only tells us that the meet of all (m,, k , ) -f m constraints is impossible if the server capacity is below a threshold. It does not tell us what is the sufficient server capacity for meeting all (m,, k,). fm constraints. Therefore for providing deterministic guarantee, a sufficient condition is fundamental.

div.head: NP-DBP-EDF scheduling algorithm
div.p: We note by DBP,(t) the value of DBP of job j at time point f. Under NP-DBP-EDF scheduling policy, at time f, the instance, which is being executed in the unique server, has highest priority because of the non pre-emption. The instances waiting for their execution at time tare served in order of their DBP priorities. The instances with DBP>(t) = 1 (for j = I , 2. n) must be executed before their deadlines, othenvise their (m,,kJf m constraint guarantee will be violated. Instances with DBP,(t) >I will be executed if they can get the server and can be finished before their deadlines, otherwise they are discarded We recall that instances with the same DBP value are scheduled under EDF.

div.head: Conclusions
div.p: In this paper, we firstly recalled how (m,k)-firm model can be used to define the graceful degradation of real-time QoS and then addressed the problem of deterministic guarantee of (mk)-firm real-time requirement for a set of periodic or sporadic jobs sharing a common server. DBP has been chosen for its interesting feature of dynamically assigning priorities based on the recent state of the system (k-sequence). So it is suitable for QoS management in adaptive realtime systems and networks. Our main contribution is having given the expression of the sufficient condition under NP-DBP-EDF scheduling for deterministically guaranteeing (m,k)-firm constraint. This result is necessary for the system server capacity dimensioning.

Our on going work consists of its implementation, in terms of an admission control procedure, within IP networks (e.g. Internet-based control system, Remote control and monitoring systems based on Internet and power tine networks such as what has been proposed in REMPLI project www.rempli.org) for dynamically managing real-time QoS according to (m,k)-fm model.
